original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finite-separable-enough}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ satisfies the existence part of the valuative criterion
as in Definition \ref{definition-valuative-criterion},
\item $f$ satisfies the existence part of the valuative criterion
as in Definition \ref{definition-valuative-criterion} modified by
requiring the extension $K'/K$ to be finite separable.
\end{enumerate}
review_scope: Independent mathematical source-first comparison with pinned Stacks statement, applicable standing definitions and exact Stage B structured formulation; proofs not reviewed
hold_reason: The two conditions defer to an unresolved Definition \ref{definition-valuative-criterion}; the preface mentions extensions but not the complete universally quantified valuative diagrams, so the equivalence is not independently standalone.
proposed_correction: Expand both alternatives as universal valuative existence criteria with an arbitrary extension versus finite separable extension, and re-review the exact clauses.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-composition-valuative-criteria}
The composition of two morphisms of algebraic spaces which satisfy the
(existence part of, resp.\ uniqueness part of) the valuative criterion
satisfies the (existence part of, resp.\ uniqueness part of) the valuative
criterion.
review_scope: Independent mathematical source-first comparison with pinned Stacks statement, applicable standing definitions and exact Stage B structured formulation; proofs not reviewed
hold_reason: The hypotheses merely say 'two morphisms' satisfying the criterion, but do not require a composable pair f:X→Y and g:Y→Z; closure for existence and uniqueness requires that common middle space.
proposed_correction: Specify composable f:X→Y and g:Y→Z and separately state preservation of existence, uniqueness, and the full criterion by g∘f; obtain an independent source-first review.
